nodes.name: Au nanospheres synthesis
nodes.procedure: A 60 mL EG solution containing HAuCl4, PDDA, AgNO3, and HCl with concentration of 0.5 mM, 25 mM, 0.01 mM, and 1 mM, respectively, was vigorously stirred and then reacted at 220 °C for 2 h in an oil bath to synthesize Au nanospheres with a diameter of 56.8 ± 2.5 nm.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Au nanospheres... 60 mL EG solution containing HAuCl4, PDDA, AgNO3, and HCl... reacted at 220 °C for 2 h

nodes.name: B-MoSe2 nanoshells synthesis
nodes.procedure: In a typical synthesis, 5 mg of Au based nanoparticles (Au nanospheres) were first mixed with 20 mg of graphene in 10 ml of DI water, followed by 1 h of sonication. The mixture was then heated in an oven to completely remove DI water. 20 mg of dried mixture and 10 mg of Mo(CO)6 underwent further annealing treatment in a tube furnace at 550 °C for 0.5 h with the protection of N2 atmosphere to obtained AuMo alloy/graphene. Then the AuMo alloy/graphene was treated with Se powder as selenium source upstream in tube furnace at 550 °C for another 0.5 h in N2 atmosphere, forming Au@MoSe2/graphene structures. After removing Au core of Au@MoSe2 by etching agent of I/KI for 24 h treatment, B·MoSe2 were synthesized in high yield of approaching 100%.

nodes.procedure: A 60 ml EG solution containing HAuCl4, PDDA, and AgNO3 with concentration of 0.5 mM, 25 mM, and 1.6 mM, respectively, was vigorously stirred and then reacted at 220 °C for 72 h in oil bath.

nodes.name: Au nanoplates synthesis
nodes.procedure: 8 mL DI water, 1.6 mL of 0.1 M CTAC, 75 μL of 0.01 M KI, 80 μL of 25 mM HAuCl4, and 20 μL of 0.1 M NaOH were mixed to obtain a yellowish solution. 100 μL of 0.05 M ascorbic acid (AA) was then injected into the solution. After that, 10 μL of 0.1 M KOH was injected to the solution. The reaction completed in 10 min.
nodes.source_text: To synthesize the Au nanoplates, 8 mL DI water, 1.6 mL of 0.1 M CTAC... The reaction completed in 10 min

nodes.name: U-MoSe2 synthesis
nodes.procedure: 5 mg of Au@Ag nanorods were mixed with 20 mg of graphene in 10 ml of DI water, sonicated for 1 h, dried in oven, then underwent sequential annealing with 10 mg Mo(CO)6 at 550 °C for 0.5 h (N2), followed by Se powder treatment at 550 °C for 0.5 h (N2), and finally Au/Ag core removal by I/KI etching for 24 h, using similar strategies as B-MoSe2.
nodes.source_text: we further fabricated uniaxially strained (U·MoSe2)... using similar strategies (Fig. 2h–k and Supplementary Figs. 9–12)

nodes.name: F-MoSe2 synthesis
nodes.procedure: Using Au nanoplates instead of Au nanospheres, the same procedure as B-MoSe2 synthesis was followed.
nodes.source_text: we further fabricated uniaxially strained (U⋅MoSe2) and flat (F⋅MoSe2) MoSe2 without strain using similar strategies

nodes.characterization_summary: B·MoSe2 shows monodispersed hollow nanoshells with average diameter of 56.8 ± 2.5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images emphasize that the product is characterized by monodispersed hollow nanoshells with an average diameter of 56.8 ± 2.5 nm (Fig. 2a and Supplementary Figs. 5–7).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals uniform few-atomic thick layers and atomically curved MoSe2 with (002) plane spacing of 0.69 nm for B·MoSe2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) image reveals the uniform few-atomic thick layers and the atomically curved MoSe2 from the cross-sectional view (Fig. 2b, c).

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-HAADF-STEM confirms 2H-MoSe2 hexagonal lattice arrangement of Mo and Se atoms and abundant Se vacancies in B·MoSe2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-HAADF-STEM) confirms the existence of 2H-MoSe2, which resolves a characteristic hexagonal lattice arrangement of Mo (brighter dots) and Se (darker dots) atoms (Fig. 2d and Supplementary Fig. 8).

nodes.characterization_summary: GPA shows uniform biaxial strain of ~1.2% in B·MoSe2 nanoshells.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The obvious evenly color can be observed in the strain mapping, indicating the atomic curvature generates a uniform biaxial strain of ~1.2%.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows uniform distribution of Mo and Se elements in B·MoSe2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM and the corresponding EDS mapping images show the uniform distribution of Mo and Se elements (Fig. 2g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman confirms 2H phase of MoSe2 with A1g mode blueshift increasing with strain dimension.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectrum confirms the 2H phase of MoSe2 of samples, indicating the strain does not change the crystal phase (Fig. 3a).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Mo 3d5/2 binding energies blueshifting from 228.8 eV (F-MoSe2) to 228.9 eV (U-MoSe2) to 229.1 eV (B-MoSe2); Se 3d5/2 shifts to lower energy (54.33 eV) in B-MoSe2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: With increasing the strain dimension from F·MoSe2, U·MoSe2 to B·MoSe2, the binding energy of 3d5/2 gradually blueshifts from 228.8, 228.9 to 229.1 eV... the Se 3d5/2 peaks of B·MoSe2 shift to lower binding energy (54.33 eV) when compared to those of F·MoSe2 (54.54 eV) and U-MoSe2 (54.47 eV), as shown in Fig. 3c.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo K-edge XANES shows average oxidation states of +4.17 (F), +4.34 (U), +4.45 (B-MoSe2) and d-band hole counts of 8.07, 8.34, 8.45 respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The oxidation states can be estimated to be +4.17 for F·MoSe2, +4.34 for U-MoSe2, and +4.45 for B·MoSe2, using MoSe2 (4d2) and MoO3 (4d0) as references (Fig. 3e).

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS shows Mo-Se coordination numbers decreasing from 5.9 (F) to 4.4 (U) to 4.1 (B-MoSe2) and elongated Mo-Mo bonds in strained samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Mo-Se coordination numbers of F·MoSe2, U-MoSe2, and B·MoSe2 are 5.9, 4.4, and 4.1, respectively, which are lower than that (6) of MoSe2 foil (Supplementary Fig. 14).

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows enhanced signal intensity at g=2.009 for U- and B-MoSe2 confirming higher Se vacancy concentration in B·MoSe2 than U·MoSe2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EPR signal intensity at g = 2.009 of F·MoSe2 approaches 0, while those of U-MoSe2 and B·MoSe2 are drastically enhanced.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV shows Cdl of 34.3 mF cm^-2 for B·MoSe2, highest ECSA among samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The B·MoSe2 catalyst displays the highest Cdl value of 34.3 mF cm^-2 among the other two samples, implying the highest ECSA and more accessible active sites.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows charge-transfer resistance Rct of 11.6 Ω (B), 30.5 Ω (U), 45.2 Ω (F-MoSe2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The charge-transfer resistance (Rct) of the B·MoSe2, U·MoSe2, and F·MoSe2 electrode was measured to be 11.6, 30.5, and 45.2 Ω.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Raman shows transition of K+·H2O (8.9% to 2.1%) to 4HB·H2O (45.7% to 56.0%) on B·MoSe2 from 0 to -0.5 V; Stark tuning rate 23.2 cm^-1/V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As the applied potentials negatively increases from 0 to -0.5 V, the content of K+·H2O on the surface of B·MoSe2 decreases from 8.9% to 2.1%, while that of 4HB·H2O increases from 45.7% to 56.0%.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS confirms stable Mo/Se molar ratio approaching 1/2 after durability test.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) indicates the molar ratio of Mo/Se was still approaching 1/2, verifying the stable structures (Supplementary Table 3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Powder XRD data collected using Cu Kα radiation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Philips X'pert Pro X-ray diffractometer equipped with Cu Kα radiation (λ = 0.15419 nm) was used to obtain powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) data.
